title: What a Shipped Binary Owes: The Licence of Each Qt Module You Link, How You Link It, and What You Must Hand Over

questions.question: Most Qt modules a control station uses are offered under which open source licence?
options: The LGPL 3.0, with conditions about how they are linked and what is shipped
questions.explanation: Core, Gui, Widgets, Network, Qml and Quick were LGPL in the table.

questions.question: A program links Charts and is given to a customer. What follows?
options: It is the GPL 3.0 as a whole, with its source, or needs a commercial licence
questions.explanation: Charts is offered under the GPL 3.0 only or a commercial licence.

questions.question: Why must the LGPL modules be linked dynamically?
options: The person who has the program must be able to replace Qt with another build
questions.explanation: A static link was a finding.

questions.question: A module is not in the table. What does licence_of say?
Qt6Charts, Charts and QtCharts are in one list. How many findings do they make?
options: One: the name is the same once it is made lowercase and its prefix taken off
questions.explanation: A module spelt three ways was one finding.

questions.question: Is this lesson legal advice?
options: No: it is a table to start from, and the licence of the Qt that is shipped is what counts
questions.explanation: The lesson says so at the top and under what it does not do.
